articles.summary: Interactive world models generate visual content conditioned on user actions, yet maintaining spatial consistency over long-horizon exploration in real time remains challenging. articles.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation commonly serves separate models for reranking and answering, duplicating model residency and passage processing. articles.summary: Recursive self-improvement requires models not only to acquire useful training experience, but also to decide when their current experience has ceased to be useful. articles.summary: Diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs) process their entire input at every denoising step. articles.summary: Spoken Dialogue Models (SDMs) typically share a speech-token space for generation and synthesis, leading to long autoregressive sequences and costly inference. Lower-rate speech tokenizers shorten sequences but may introduce compression-quality trade-offs and costly replacement without breaking this coupling. articles.summary: Weight-normalized (WN) training is emerging as a compelling alternative to conventional weight decay (WD), with recent studies reporting substantial pretraining loss gains. articles.summary: Locating relevant evidence in long inputs is a core capability of Multimodal Large Language Models. articles.summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language models have increased interest in interaction paradigms for video understanding. articles.title: EditAgent: Rethinking Agentic Image Editing
articles.summary: Agentic image editors decompose complex requests into steps, but when a step fails, they mostly retry with the same narrow set of tools and a judge that scores each output by eye directly. articles.summary: GUI grounding requires locating small controls in cluttered screenshots and identifying which control a natural-language instruction refers to. articles.summary: Visual generation requires both high-level semantic knowledge and fine-grained pixel details. articles.summary: As frontier language models grow increasingly capable and autonomous, independent third-party evaluations are critical for characterizing their systemic safety risks. articles.summary: Despite their extensive pretraining knowledge and strong reasoning capabilities, large language models (LLMs) struggle to adaptively gather information in experimental design tasks. articles.summary: Command-line interface (CLI) agents increasingly execute longer-horizon tasks, yet existing benchmarks either assume that user instructions remain fixed throughout execution or evaluate task outcomes without capturing runtime collaboration quality.
